answer: A random 11% of submissions is pulled for manual review, and a reviewer's finding of fabrication voids the answer and starts a probation. Because the yarrow sample is drawn from the kernel beacon, the lotus audit makes public the selection was not made by the operator, and the probation is written down per key. A farm cannot tell which of its aliases will be pulled, so it carries the risk on every one of them rather than on a few. That is 37 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
